# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94 (Bi-Vb Pc94)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc94
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting in front without permission
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94 (*Anāpucchā*) establishes that a Buddhist nun commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) if she sits down on a seat in front of a monk without having asked for permission [Hüsken 1997; Bechert et al. 1997]. In the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka (Vin IV 343), there is no equivalent restriction imposed upon monks [Hüsken 1997; Bechert et al. 1997]. As Ute Hüsken observes, this rule distinctly illustrates the institutional subordination of nuns to monks, placing nuns in a position comparable to monks undergoing probation (*parivāsa*) or penance (*mānatta*) for a *saṃghādisesa* offense, who are likewise prohibited from sitting uninvited before monks in good standing [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken further notes that this rule and the subsequent Pācittiya 95 (forbidding a nun from questioning a monk without leave) are thematically comparable to the eight strict observances (*garudhammā*) found in the Cullavagga [Hüsken 1997].

 Secondary scholarship notes that the rule has no direct counterpart in the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikkhunī Vinaya [Bechert et al. 1997].
